inflection_points.summary: fix: drop the scaffold's opener capability
inflection_points.body:
create-tauri-app left opener:default in the capabilities — permission to
open arbitrary URLs and reveal paths in the OS explorer — which the spec
never granted. Plugin, crate, and demo command removed with it.

inflection_points.summary: fix: make paths and photo parsing platform-neutral
inflection_points.body:
paths.ts split only on '/', so a Windows layout path collapsed dirname
to '.' and every font resolved against the wrong directory, silently.

photos.ts still parsed headers through Node's Buffer, which does not
exist in a webview. Both parsers now use Uint8Array and DataView, and a
test proves buildPhotoIndex runs with the Buffer global removed.

inflection_points.summary: refactor: move engine file I/O behind a FileSystem interface
inflection_points.body:
The engine must run inside the Tauri webview. Its five Node I/O calls
now go through FileSystem, implemented by Node for the CLI and tests.
No behaviour change; the existing suite passes unchanged.

inflection_points.summary: docs: editor design around typed markers; overflow ladder; stale fixes
inflection_points.body:
Section 6 now describes the authoring model the operator chose: a drawn
box for the photo, a typed run of x for each text field (position, font,
size and width in one gesture), colour and alignment as field properties,
one marker per line for multi-line fields, and a per-field cover toggle so
the template's own placeholders never have to be edited out in CorelDRAW.

TextStyle matches the engine as built (fontId, overflow). The overflow
ladder documents abbreviate-then-shrink and its known limit.

Section 5 records that the engine must run inside the webview behind an
I/O seam. Section 7.5 no longer says 'warn below 300dpi'. The plan's
normaliseId listing carries an execution note pointing at the fix.

inflection_points.summary: fix: implement the date transform and close operator-facing gaps
inflection_points.body:
Second wave of the final whole-branch review (F4, F6, three operator-facing
gaps, and four minors).

- F4: applyTransform gains a real 'date' case (src/card.ts), parsing
  DD.MM.YYYY, DD/MM/YYYY, DD-MM-YYYY and ISO YYYY-MM-DD, and formatting per
  binding.format (DD/MM/YYYY/YY tokens, default DD.MM.YYYY). An unparseable
  value passes through unchanged rather than throwing or printing a mangled
  date. Previously the fixture's DOB only looked correct by coincidence.

- F6: the CLI now resolves layout.fonts against the layout file's own
  directory, exactly like templateFront/templateBack, so a project folder
  with relative font paths stays self-contained regardless of the process's
  cwd. fonts.ts is unchanged.

- Operator-facing gaps: a missing --photos directory is now a distinct,
  named error (PhotoDirectoryNotFoundError) instead of silently becoming
  1000 photo-missing issues; the CLI prints job-backs.pdf alongside
  job-fronts.pdf whenever a back side is rendered; an empty spreadsheet is
  refused with a clear message before anything is written, instead of
  silently producing a zero-page PDF.

- Minors: package.json drops npm-init boilerplate (main, directories) and
  gains engines.node >=22; fixtures/layout.json drops the unused 'label'
  font; the fitText boxWidth<=0 comment no longer overstates what its
  maxLines slice does; flipY gets a direct unit test; the photo-collision
  test now asserts which file actually won.

105/105 tests passing, tsc clean. Report appended to
.superpowers/sdd/final-review-fixes.md (Wave 2).

inflection_points.summary: fix: align overlay baselines and close silent-rescale paths
inflection_points.body:
Fixes six findings from the final whole-branch review.

F1 (most important): every overlay baseline sat 2.05pt below the
template's own label baseline. Two causes. (a) drawCard anchored the
baseline on the shrunk font size (fit.size) instead of the element's
designed size (style.size), so shrink-to-fit moved the baseline and
neighbouring cards whose text did/didn't shrink disagreed on it.
Fixed by anchoring on style.size always. (b) fixtures/layout.json's
box.y values had been derived against pdf-lib 1.17.1's buggy
heightAtSize(size, {descender:false}), which silently returns the
wrong ascent for any font whose unitsPerEm isn't 1000 (true for this
project's TrueType fonts). A prior task fixed ascentAtSize to read
the real ascent from the fontkit font object, but nobody re-derived
the fixture's box.y against the corrected value, which had been
quietly agreeing with the bug's ~2.05pt-low answer. Corrected all
nine text elements' box.y by -2.0545pt, documented the box.y contract
on elementSchema/TextStyle in layout.ts, and recorded the measured-y
-> box.y conversion in the spec's Appendix A. Added a rasterized
baseline-pinning test plus a shrink-vs-no-shrink baseline-parity
test, both proven to discriminate by temporarily reverting each
cause.

F2: renderJob now throws when solveGrid picks a rotated orientation,
since drawCard has no way to draw a rotated card and would otherwise
silently crop every card on the sheet.

F3: renderJob now reads each template's real page size before
drawing and throws if the front differs from layout.pageBox, or the
back differs from the front, by more than 0.5pt in either axis --
closing the silent 2x-rescale path the cell clip was hiding.

F5: drawCard now clips text elements with fit: 'clip' to their own
box, the same way the photo branch already clips -- fitText's clip
mode reports overflow but never truncates the string itself.

F7: added --flip <axis> to the render CLI command (long-edge or
short-edge, defaulting to long-edge, rejecting anything else),
wired through to renderJob's flipAxis. cli.ts also gained an
entry-point guard so it stays safely importable by tests.

Minor 7: valignOffset is clamped at 0 so a text block taller than
its box can no longer draw upward into the row above.

inflection_points.summary: fix: cover the duplex mirror, tighten the content check, scope photo embeds
inflection_points.body:
No test produced a back PDF, so a renderJob that never mirrored would
have passed the whole suite — on the one function whose failure ruins
every card in a duplex run.

The 'renders real content' check counted the transparent page background,
so a card renderer that drew nothing satisfied it.

Every photo in the index was embedded into every side, including ids not
in the job and sides with no photo element, shipping children's
photographs to a print vendor for no reason.

inflection_points.summary: fix: keep crop marks out of neighbouring cards
inflection_points.body:
Marks extended a fixed 8pt from every card edge regardless of available
room. On a butt-cut grid that put ink inside the adjacent card, and on a
tight margin it produced a negative coordinate off the sheet. Both grid
shapes solveGrid actually produces.

Mark geometry is now a pure function clamped to the space each edge has,
omitting interior marks entirely where two cards touch.

inflection_points.summary: fix: make preflight dpi messages self-consistent, pin the blank-id guard
inflection_points.body:
A photo at 149.69dpi reported as 'photo is 150dpi at printed size, below
the 150dpi floor' — the comparison was right but the displayed number was
rounded to look wrong, which is how an operator learns to distrust the
whole report.

The guard stopping a blank-id row from also reporting a missing photo had
no committed test, and the duplicate-id message said 'row' while listing
several.

inflection_points.summary: fix: validate PNG headers and report photo id collisions
inflection_points.body:
A non-PNG file named .png returned fabricated dimensions (1094795585)
that would have passed the print-resolution gate as astronomically high
rather than failing it.

Two files whose stems normalise to the same id silently discarded one of
them, which is how a student ends up with someone else's face on their
card. Collisions are now recorded and the winner is deterministic.

effectiveDpi returned Infinity for a degenerate box, passing every gate
instead of failing them.

inflection_points.summary: test: pin the hard-break floor across multiple lines
inflection_points.body:
Three of the five termination tests passed against the pre-fix code; only
the sub-glyph and negative-width cases were load-bearing. Nothing covered
the floor being re-entered on later lines, which is where a refactor of
wrap would most plausibly reintroduce the hang.

The non-positive-box guard also returned lines ignoring maxLines, unlike
the other two overflow paths.

inflection_points.summary: fix: make fitText total, and pin its termination cases
inflection_points.body:
A negative box width let wrap() spin on an empty word and then throw
RangeError from the unbounded fallback, instead of returning overflow.

None of the five termination cases had a committed test, including the
one that originally hung; the existing unbreakable-token test does not
reach the hard-break floor and passes against the unfixed code.

fit:'wrap' was indistinguishable from fit:'shrink'. It now wraps at the
design size without shrinking, as its name says.

normaliseId mapped a blank id to '0', colliding with a genuine id of zero
and making findDuplicateIds report blank rows as duplicates.

normaliseHeader's curly-apostrophe fold was flattened to an ASCII no-op
during transcription, and its test was flattened the same way so it could
not fail. Both now use ’ escapes.

A failed formula cell rendered as the literal string [object Object],
which would have been printed onto a card.
